song.title: Hide Away
song.album: Let's Hide Away and Dance Away with Freddy King (1961) — originally issued as a Federal single, 1960/61

guitar.evidence: Multiple independent guitar-history sources place King on a Gibson Les Paul Goldtop with P-90 pickups during this specific 1960 King/Federal Records period, corroborated by a contemporary photo (Chicago, 1959) showing him with the goldtop. His signature Gibson ES-345/ES-355 is documented as a later-career instrument (from 'Bonanza of Instrumentals' onward), not this session.
guitar.notes: Played fingerstyle with a plastic thumbpick and metal index fingerpick. One low-authority secondhand account suggests both pickups blended, volumes near half — unconfirmed, kept as a note only.
guitar.source: fundamental-changes.com — Freddie King artist profile; jonmaclennan.com — 'The Ultimate Hide Away Guitar Lesson'; TDPRI forum — 'What was Freddie King's amp on Hide Away/Dance Away'

tone.target: raw tweed-Fender-driven blues shuffle lead, natural amp breakup, King Records chamber-echo ambience (studio version, Aug 26 1960)
tone.profile: raw tweed-Fender-driven blues shuffle lead, natural amp breakup, King Records chamber-echo ambience
tone.summary: Clean signal chain relying entirely on amp-driven grit from a tweed-era Fender combo (exact model unconfirmed), P-90 goldtop midrange snarl, and the King Records concrete-block echo chamber ambience — no overdrive pedal, no chorus, no Fender spring reverb (didn't exist commercially until 1961) or distinct slapback delay on this specific 1960 recording.
avoid: OD/fuzz pedal (no commercial overdrive pedal existed in 1960)
Fender spring reverb character (6G15 unit launched 1961, after this session)
gearClues: King Records concrete-block echo chamber ambience
corrections: removed ES-345 as primary guitar for this session — documented later in King's career, not on Hide Away (1960)
removed PRE overdrive (Green OD) — no commercial OD pedals existed in 1960; grit comes from amp gain only
removed Chorus/modulation block — anachronistic and undocumented
replaced Spring reverb with Room — ambience is King Studio's physical echo chamber; Fender's spring reverb (6G15) launched in 1961
removed Slapback delay — the echo is chamber ambience across the whole mix, not an isolated guitar repeat
downgraded AMP/CAB matchQuality to 'acceptable' — exact tweed model (Twin/Bassman/Pro/Deluxe) unconfirmed, catalog-constrained approximation

blocks.gap: Catalog only offers 'US Deluxe' for tweed-family tone; real amp was likely larger (Twin/Bassman) per forum accounts, but unconfirmed and outside the given catalog.

blocks.purpose: Modern mixing/finishing tool on the modeled rig, not part of the original 1960 chain.
